clue.text: Sort of acid spitefulness cut short

indicators.note: cut short says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: malice is spitefulness, the wish to do harm

explanation.surface: Someone's spiteful remark is stopped before it finishes, with a chemistry aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Malic acid is the sharp-tasting organic acid found in apples, so the word names a sort of acid.

clue.text: Converters seen in spacecraft's flight to stars

parts.note: a space mission is a spacecraft's flight
Aries is a constellation of stars, the Ram

explanation.surface: People who change others' views are spotted on a rocket journey to the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Missionaries seek to convert people to their religion, so they are converters.

clue.text: Heading off to draw out what's permitted

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, permitted, with what's as filler

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter is removed

parts.note: to elicit is to draw out a response

explanation.surface: Someone diverts a question in order to extract what's allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit means lawful or allowed, the opposite of illicit.

clue.text: Macho sort misused Internet sites

indicators.note: misused suggests the letters are put to wrong use, scrambled

explanation.surface: A macho type abuses websites.
explanation.definitionFit: Chat rooms are online sites where users exchange messages in real time.

clue.text: Order put in by one procuring scented ball

indicators.note: put in by says the honour's letters are placed inside the procurer's word

parts.note: a pander is one who procures, a pimp or go-between
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An instruction is given by someone obtaining a perfumed ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomander is a perforated ball or container of perfume or spices, carried or hung to scent the air.

clue.text: Advance I am making here and there

parts.note: to pass is to advance or go forward
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone moves forward while doing things in various places.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim is Latin used in references to mean throughout, appearing here and there.

clue.text: An incurable optimist, I run webcam terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are handled badly, rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A hopeful person confesses to operating a webcam badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Micawber, from Dickens's David Copperfield, always believes something will turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkins Micawber is the Dickens character who stays hopeful despite poverty, so his name stands for a hopeless optimist.

clue.text: Opera's not quite up to standard

indicators.note: not quite says the last letter is removed

parts.note: normal means at the usual standard

explanation.surface: A critic says an opera falls a little short of standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Bellini's opera about a Druid priestess.

clue.text: Point to man in black as worthy of respect

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: in says the man's name goes inside the word for black

parts.note: sable is black in heraldry
Tim is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone points to a man in black clothes as deserving respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimable means deserving of esteem, worthy of respect.

clue.text: Welfare system made when party has a financial asset

parts.note: a social is a party or gathering
a security is a financial asset such as a bond or share

explanation.surface: A benefits scheme is set up when a political party owns an investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Social security is the state scheme of welfare payments to the unemployed, sick and elderly.

clue.text: Could the man I ditched become sloppy?

indicators.note: ditched become says the words are cast aside and turned into something new

explanation.surface: A jilted partner wonders whether being dumped will make them careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmethodical means without method, careless and disorganized, so sloppy.

clue.text: Contend in cold weather, with wife the last to ask questions

indicators.note: in says the word for contend goes inside the other piece
the last says the wife's letter moves to the end of the cold-weather word

parts.note: winter is the season of cold weather
to vie is to contend or compete

explanation.surface: Someone struggles through a freezing spell while his wife gets the final word in questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with wife the last' sends the W from the front to the back, giving INTERW; the definition is a verb phrase, so 'to ask questions' swaps for the verb sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To interview someone is to put questions to them, as a journalist or employer does.

clue.text: Present-day graduate's new commercial handler

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era of dates
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A recent graduate's fresh job is handling advertising accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: An adman works in advertising, handling and creating commercials for clients.

clue.text: Element admitting 20 with no opposition

indicators.note: admitting says the element lets the other letters in

parts.note: neon is a chemical element, a noble gas
20-across is a master of ceremonies, abbreviated MC

explanation.surface: A chemical element accepts something numbered twenty without any objection.
explanation.walkthrough: NEM CON is Latin nemine contradicente, 'nobody contradicting', used of a vote passed with no one against.
explanation.definitionFit: Nem con is the formal Latin phrase for a motion carried without a single dissenting vote.

clue.text: Dealing with small particles of gold piece left in tooth

indicators.note: in says the coin and left go inside the tooth

parts.note: a molar is a back tooth
an ecu was an old French gold coin

explanation.surface: A dentist finds a gold filling in a tooth and studies the tiny particles.
explanation.definitionFit: Molecular means relating to molecules, the small particles of matter.

clue.text: As food is on time, be here?

definitions.text: As food is on time, be here?

parts.words: As food is on time, be here?
parts.note: when the meal served in the late afternoon is ready, this piece of furniture is where it gets laid out

explanation.surface: A wry question about where to be when the meal arrives punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea table is a small table at which afternoon tea is served, so food at teatime is on it.

clue.text: Correspond about old photo in current fashion

indicators.note: about says the correspond word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to tally is to correspond or match
pic is short for picture, a photo

explanation.surface: Someone exchanges letters about an old photograph in the modern way.
explanation.definitionFit: Topically means in a way relating to current affairs, matching the matters of the moment.

clue.text: Live animal covering top of hump in sauce

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: covering says the animal goes round the other letter

parts.note: a camel is an animal with a hump

indicators.note: top of says the first letter of the hump is taken

explanation.surface: A living camel with a hump is found in a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Bechamel is a white sauce made from a roux of butter and flour with milk.

clue.text: Gets satisfaction from banks keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping says the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them, so banks means relies
SH is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in financial institutions that stay discreet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, as in 'banks on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to enjoy it, to get satisfaction or pleasure from it.

clue.text: Look briefly into school to give a talk

indicators.note: into says the shortened look goes inside the school abbreviation
briefly says the word for look loses its last letter

parts.note: to peek is to look quickly

explanation.surface: A visitor glances quickly into a school in order to deliver an address.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech is a formal talk delivered to an audience.

clue.text: City's former network brought up

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue says the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a rete is a network of nerves or blood vessels

explanation.surface: A city's old system has been raised for discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is the cathedral city of Devon in south-west England.

clue.text: Gallantry award announced for show director

indicators.note: announced says the letters are spoken aloud, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: MC is the Military Cross, a British award for gallantry

explanation.surface: A medal for bravery is proclaimed for the person running a show.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee is a master of ceremonies, the host who presents and directs a show.

clue.text: Principle essential to the thickest

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A principle that matters most to the least intelligent people.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral principle or set of values guiding conduct.

clue.text: Spell with a Conservative crowd endlessly making notes

parts.note: a hex is a spell or curse

indicators.note: endlessly says the crowd word loses its final letter

parts.note: a horde is a large crowd

explanation.surface: A Tory casts a spell on a crowd while writing music.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexachord is a series of six notes, a scale unit in early music theory.

clue.text: Decided on part to be included in dictionary

indicators.note: to be included in says the part's letters go inside the dictionary

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: An editor decided which section should go into the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose, so opted means decided.

clue.text: I do all the match preparation for this team

indicators.note: preparation suggests the words are worked up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A groundsman or kit man boasts of readying everything for a match day.
explanation.walkthrough: Oldham Athletic is an English football club from Oldham, near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldham Athletic is a professional football club, so it is a team.

clue.text: Lorry driver overtaking learner, one who was crawling

indicators.note: overtaking says the driver takes the learner's letter inside

parts.note: a trucker drives a lorry, the British word for a truck
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A lorry driver passes a learner driver, who was moving very slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawling' here means being servile, not moving slowly in traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A truckler submits or fawns to those above, so he is one who crawls obsequiously.

clue.text: No mark for melody transcribed for unusual singing

indicators.note: transcribed suggests the remaining letters are rewritten in a new order
no says the letter for mark is taken away

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A tune is written out for an odd vocal performance, with no mark awarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Yodelling is a distinctive style of singing that flips between chest voice and falsetto.
